habitat: Palm savanna with Borassus and Hyphaene palms. It forages on the ground and droops its wings while pumping its tail.
summary: A common localised resident. It has a black-bordered throat patch, often broken, a grey nape, and a long rufous tail. The eyes are straw-coloured. The song is melodious and liquid. Avibase marks it rare, so the months are left unset. The Kemp name Collared Palm Thrush and the code VB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: Black-bordered throat patch, often broken or incomplete. Grey nape. The eyes are straw-coloured.

upperparts.pattern: Duller mantle than Rufous-tailed Palm Thrush.

viewNotes.note: Black-bordered throat patch and a grey nape.

calls.description: A melodious liquid song, mostly mornings and evenings. No South African grade A recording was found. The grade A song is from Mida Creek in Kenya. The filename is XC791944-20230407-082501_Collared-Palm-Thrush_Mida-Creek_edited.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common localised resident. Avibase marks Collared Palm-Thrush rare, so the months are left unset. Straw-coloured is not a colour name, so the iris is left unset. The grade A song is from Kenya. The Kemp name Collared Palm Thrush and the code VB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^3=8 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 4–16.
